SEARCH
Package neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline.twophasepipe

Class TwoFluidConservationEquations

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline.twophasepipe.TwoFluidConservationEquations
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class TwoFluidConservationEquations extends Object implements Serializable
Two-fluid conservation equations for transient multiphase pipe flow.

Implements the spatial discretization of the two-fluid model equations:

Conservation Equations

  • Gas Mass: ∂/∂t(α_g·ρ_g·A) + ∂/∂x(α_g·ρ_g·v_g·A) = Γ_g
  • Liquid Mass: ∂/∂t(α_L·ρ_L·A) + ∂/∂x(α_L·ρ_L·v_L·A) = Γ_L
  • Gas Momentum: ∂/∂t(α_g·ρ_g·v_g·A) + ∂/∂x(α_g·ρ_g·v_g²·A) = -α_g·A·∂P/∂x - τ_wg·S_g - τ_i·S_i - α_g·ρ_g·g·A·sin(θ)
  • Liquid Momentum: ∂/∂t(α_L·ρ_L·v_L·A) + ∂/∂x(α_L·ρ_L·v_L²·A) = -α_L·A·∂P/∂x - τ_wL·S_L + τ_i·S_i - α_L·ρ_L·g·A·sin(θ)
  • Mixture Energy: ∂/∂t(E_mix·A) + ∂/∂x((E_mix+P)·v_mix·A) = Q_wall + W_friction

Variable Indices

  • 0: Gas mass per length (α_g·ρ_g·A)
  • 1: Liquid mass per length (α_L·ρ_L·A)
  • 2: Gas momentum per length (α_g·ρ_g·v_g·A)
  • 3: Liquid momentum per length (α_L·ρ_L·v_L·A)
  • 4: Mixture energy per length (E_mix·A)

    • enableWaterOilSlip

      private boolean enableWaterOilSlip
      Enable water-oil velocity slip (7-equation model). When true, oil and water have separate momentum equations allowing different velocities.

    • enableInterfacialPressure

      private boolean enableInterfacialPressure
      Enable the non-conservative holdup-gradient momentum term, including the interfacial pressure correction that keeps the two-fluid system hyperbolic.

      Off by default. The term removes the sustained phase backflow and the unbounded liquid packing that liquid-rich lines otherwise show, but it is acoustic in scale and is evaluated explicitly, so it needs a CFL number near 0.05 rather than the default 0.5. Enabling it without also tightening the CFL diverges. Completing it means folding the term into the implicit pressure solve of the IMEX integrator.

    • implicitInterfacialPressure

      private boolean implicitInterfacialPressure
      Whether the Bestion stabilizer is handled by the time integrator instead of the explicit RHS.

    • interfacialPressureCoefficient

      private double interfacialPressureCoefficient
      Interfacial pressure coefficient delta in the Bestion closure. The two-fluid system has real characteristics for delta greater than or equal to one; a value slightly above one leaves margin. Reference: Bestion, D. (1990), "The physical closure laws in the CATHARE code", Nuclear Engineering and Design 124, 229-245.

    • outletBackflowClamped

      private boolean outletBackflowClamped
      Whether the transmissive outlet has had to suppress a reversed phase velocity.

      Sticky once set, so a caller can ask after a sequence of steps. Cleared with clearOutletBackflowClamped().

      private boolean enableVirtualMassForce
      Enable virtual mass force term in momentum equations. The virtual mass force accounts for the inertia of the displaced phase during rapid acceleration/deceleration. Reference: Drew, D.A. and Lahey, R.T. (1987), "The virtual mass and lift force on a sphere in rotating and straining inviscid flow", Int. J. Multiphase Flow.

    • calcRHS

      public double[][] calcRHS(TwoFluidSection[] sections, double dx)
      Calculate the right-hand side (dU/dt) for all cells.

      This is the main entry point for the numerical integration. Returns the time derivative of conservative variables for each cell.

      Parameters:
      sections - Array of pipe sections with current state
      dx - Cell size (m) — used as uniform dx; for non-uniform mesh each section's own length is used via sections[i].getLength()
      Returns:
      Time derivatives [nCells][NUM_EQUATIONS]

    • accumulateLastPhaseMassFaceFluxes

      public void accumulateLastPhaseMassFaceFluxes(double[][] accumulator, double weight)
      Add the most recently evaluated phase-resolved face mass flows to a caller-owned accumulator.

      This avoids allocating a defensive snapshot for every Runge-Kutta stage while keeping the retained internal buffer encapsulated. The accumulator must have shape [sections.length + 1][3] for the most recent calcRHS(TwoFluidSection[], double) evaluation.

      Parameters:
      accumulator - destination receiving weight * faceMassFlow
      weight - integration-stage weight
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the accumulator shape is incompatible or the weight is not finite

    • accumulateLastPhaseMassSourcesPerLength

      public void accumulateLastPhaseMassSourcesPerLength(double[][] accumulator, double weight)
      Add the most recently evaluated cell phase-mass sources to a caller-owned accumulator.

      Rows are finite-volume cells and columns are gas, oil, and water in kg/(m s). This is the source counterpart to accumulateLastPhaseMassFaceFluxes(double[][], double) and lets component transport use the same Runge-Kutta stage weights as the accepted hydrodynamic phase masses.

      Parameters:
      accumulator - destination receiving weight * sourceRate
      weight - integration-stage weight

    • calcPhaseMassFaceFluxes

      public double[][] calcPhaseMassFaceFluxes(TwoFluidSection[] sections, double dx)
      Calculate phase-resolved mass flow at every finite-volume face from the same boundary and AUSM+ fluxes used by the conservative equations.

      Rows are faces from inlet through outlet; columns are gas, oil, and water in kg/s. A positive value points in the increasing section-index direction. CLOSED boundaries are represented by the zero boundary velocities imposed by TwoFluidPipe, so their external face flow is exactly zero while internal convection remains available.

      Parameters:
      sections - current finite-volume sections
      dx - minimum mesh spacing in metres, retained for consistency with the spatial flux API
      Returns:
      face mass flows with shape [sections.length + 1][3]
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if sections is null or empty

    • populatePhaseMassFaceFluxes

      private double[][] populatePhaseMassFaceFluxes(double[][] phaseMassFaceFluxes, int sectionCount, double[][] interfaceFluxes, double[] inletFlux, double[] outletFlux)
      Populate a caller-provided face-flux buffer, allocating only when its face count is incompatible.
      Parameters:
      phaseMassFaceFluxes - reusable destination, or null
      sectionCount - number of finite-volume sections
      interfaceFluxes - conservative fluxes at internal faces
      inletFlux - conservative inlet-face flux
      outletFlux - conservative outlet-face flux
      Returns:
      populated face mass flows with gas, oil, and water columns

    • calcInletFlux

      private double[] calcInletFlux(TwoFluidSection sec)
      Calculate inlet flux using the inlet cell state. This represents mass entering the domain from the inlet stream. Uses holdups directly (set by steady state or BC) rather than computing from mass per length to avoid feedback from cell depletion.
      Parameters:
      sec - the inlet pipe section
      Returns:
      array of flux values for each conserved variable

    • calcOutletFlux

      private double[] calcOutletFlux(TwoFluidSection sec)
      Calculate outlet flux using upwind scheme (transmissive boundary).

      By default, each reversed phase velocity is clamped at zero because a one-way transmissive boundary has no upstream state to advect in. When signed outlet flow is explicitly enabled, the zero-gradient interior phase state supplies that boundary state and a reversed phase carries signed mass and energy back into the domain. Use signed flow only with a well-posed pressure-momentum model and a boundary whose physical interpretation permits fallback.

      Parameters:
      sec - the outlet pipe section
      Returns:
      array of flux values for each conserved variable

    • calcInclinedSectionGasCarryoverNumber

      private double calcInclinedSectionGasCarryoverNumber(TwoFluidSection sec)
      Calculate a local inclined-section gas-carryover screen.

      The result contains no upstream gas volume, riser height, top pressure, or choke response and therefore must not be interpreted as a severe-slugging system criterion.

      Parameters:
      sec - local solved pipe section
      Returns:
      dimensionless gas-carryover number, or positive infinity when not applicable

    • applyInterfacialPressure

      void applyInterfacialPressure(TwoFluidSection[] sections, double[][] dUdt)
      Apply the non-conservative holdup-gradient momentum term.

      The momentum flux carries the phase pressure contribution as alpha_k * p * A, so its divergence produces p * A * d(alpha_k)/dx on top of the physical alpha_k * A * dp/dx. That extra term is spurious and must be cancelled. Cancelling it alone would leave the classical two-fluid system, which has complex characteristics and is ill-posed: short wavelengths grow without bound, which shows up as sustained phase backflow in liquid-rich flow. The standard remedy is to retain an interfacial pressure difference delta_p_i = p - p_i in the same term, giving 

       S_k += (p - delta_p_i) * A * d(alpha_k) / dx

      with the Bestion closure delta_p_i = delta * rho_g * rho_l * (u_g - u_l)^2 / (alpha_g * rho_l + alpha_l * rho_g). Because the phase fractions sum to one their gradients sum to zero, so the total momentum added over the three phases is exactly zero and the scheme stays conservative.

      Parameters:
      sections - current stage state
      dUdt - complete uncoupled conservative-variable rates, modified in place

    • calcInterfacialPressureDifference

      double calcInterfacialPressureDifference(TwoFluidSection sec)
      Get the interfacial pressure difference p - p_i from the Bestion closure.

      The characteristics of the two-fluid system are real when p - p_i is at least alpha_g * alpha_l * rho_g * rho_l * (u_g - u_l)^2 / (alpha_g * rho_l + alpha_l * rho_g), so the coefficient is that critical value scaled by delta. The alpha_g * alpha_l factor makes the term vanish in both single-phase limits, where no interfacial pressure exists.

      Parameters:
      sec - pipe section to evaluate
      Returns:
      interfacial pressure difference in pascals, never negative

    • calcVoidWaveSlipCoefficient

      public double calcVoidWaveSlipCoefficient(TwoFluidSection sec)
      Get the drift-flux slip coefficient of the interfacial pressure term.

      Converting the two phase momentum sources -delta_p_i * A * d(alpha_k)/dx into an equation for the drift flux q = alpha_g * alpha_l * (u_g - u_l) gives dq/dt = -K * d(alpha_g)/dx with K = delta_p_i * (alpha_l / rho_g + alpha_g / rho_l). That coefficient is what the implicit void-wave update needs, and it is not the same as the square of calcVoidWaveSpeed(TwoFluidSection).

      Parameters:
      sec - pipe section to evaluate
      Returns:
      slip coefficient in m2/s2, never negative

    • calcVoidWaveSpeed

      public double calcVoidWaveSpeed(TwoFluidSection sec)
      Get the void-wave speed introduced by the interfacial pressure term.

      This is the extra characteristic speed relative to the mixture velocity, and it must be included in the CFL limit once the term is active.

      Parameters:
      sec - pipe section to evaluate

    • applyVirtualMassCoupling

      void applyVirtualMassCoupling(TwoFluidSection[] sections, double[][] dUdt)
      Apply the local, stage-pure virtual-mass momentum coupling.

      The uncoupled conservative rates already contain flux divergence, pressure, gravity, friction, and transfer sources. Converting those rates to phase accelerations and solving the two-phase added-inertia relation algebraically avoids hidden velocity history and makes repeated RHS evaluations deterministic.

      Parameters:
      sections - current stage state
      dUdt - complete uncoupled conservative-variable rates, modified in place

    • applyStiffBubbleDrag

      public double[][] applyStiffBubbleDrag(TwoFluidSection[] sections, double[][] state, double timeStep)
      Advance corrected dispersed-bubble drag with a pure local implicit source solve.

      The input state is not modified. Gas and combined-liquid momentum are coupled conservatively; the liquid impulse is distributed by active oil/water mass so water-oil slip is preserved. The energy state is unchanged, making lost kinetic energy available as internal energy.

      Parameters:
      sections - sections whose primitive properties correspond to state
      state - conservative state before the drag source step
      timeStep - source-step duration in s
      Returns:
      a new conservative state after dispersed-bubble drag
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if section/state dimensions or the time step are invalid

    • calcPhaseMassTransfer

      PhaseMassTransfer calcPhaseMassTransfer(TwoFluidSection sec)
      Calculate phase-resolved mass-transfer sources for a section.

      Flash-driven transfer delegates to ThermodynamicCoupling. A prescribed evaporation source is distributed over the actual oil and water donor inventories. A prescribed condensation source has no equilibrium phase identity, so the explicitly configured hydrodynamic water cut is retained for backward compatibility.

      Parameters:
      sec - pipe section
      Returns:
      immutable phase-resolved transfer result in kg/(m s)

    • calcTransferMomentumSources

      double[] calcTransferMomentumSources(TwoFluidSection sec, PhaseMassTransfer transfer)
      Calculate transfer-only phase momentum sources using donor velocity.

      During evaporation the gas receives the momentum removed from each liquid donor. During condensation the gas loses momentum at gas velocity and each receiving liquid gains momentum at that same donor velocity. The three returned sources therefore sum to zero apart from round-off.

      Parameters:
      sec - pipe section containing phase velocities
      transfer - phase-resolved mass-transfer sources
      Returns:
      gas, oil, and water momentum sources in N/m

    • setEnableVirtualMassForce

      public void setEnableVirtualMassForce(boolean enable)
      Enable or disable the virtual mass force term.

      The virtual mass force accounts for the inertia of displaced fluid during phase acceleration. It is important for:

      • Slug initiation and propagation
      • Rapid transients (valve closures, ramp-ups)
      • Wave growth and slug frequency prediction

      Reference: Drew, D.A. and Lahey, R.T. (1987), Int. J. Multiphase Flow.

      Parameters:
      enable - true to enable virtual mass force
